column2: it will not happen. Or it may

column1: happen with an unexpected result.
That result is that the application will be reading the main buffer
instead of the snapshot buffer. That is because when the snapshot occurs
the main and snapshot buffers are swapped. But the reader has a descriptor
still pointing to the buffer that it originally connected to.
This is fine for the main buffer readers
column2: as they may be blocked waiting

column1: for a watermark to be hit
main readers want is now on the snapshot buffer.
But for waiters of the snapshot buffer
column2: they are waiting for an event to

column1: occur that will trigger the snapshot and they can then consume it quickly
to save the snapshot before the next snapshot occurs. But to do this
need to read the new snapshot buffer
column2: not the old one that is now

column1: receiving new data.
Also
column2: it does not make sense to have a watermark ""buffer_percent"" on the

column1: snapshot buffer
column2: as the snapshot buffer is static and does not receive new

column1: data except all at once.
